text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the on-prem packaging RFC — I want to surface a short list of agent bootstrap / rollout risks for air-gapped sites and propose mitigations. putting it here so we can iterate.
kevin: +1, curious which of these you think are highest priority
maria: Top concerns I see: 1) corrupted/malicious delta bundles, 2) partial apply leaving agent in bad state, 3) time/skew & replay attacks affecting signature checks, 4) operator stuck because telemetry blocked by airgap, 5) storage exhaustion mid-upgrade
sachin: For (1) can we force dual-signature: vendor sig + customer offline key? makes verification require both.
anita: customer key sounds good but ops will want rollback without restoring keystore. need a fallback path.
maria: agree. proposal: require vendor signature always; customer signature optional but if present, must match. plus a per-bundle provenance file with a signed manifest listing component hashes. verify step is mandatory before any apply.
dave: what about atomicity? single-file swap vs copy-and-symlink? if apply fails halfway container might crash.
olivia: use dual-image swap: write new rootfs to alternate location, run verification, then atomically switch pointer. keep N previous images (configurable) for rollback.
kevin: That uses a lot of disk. For constrained devices we could stream-verify chunks and write to staging with an integrity journal so we can resume or abort cleanly.
sachin: add a low-disk mode: skip keeping full image but write a tiny recovery shim that can fetch a delta from a pre-staged mirror when restored (mirror must be pre-provisioned before patch window).
build-bot: deploy-bot: canary started on cluster:edge-site-07 — bundle v2024.10.3, staged -> 2 nodes
anita: Canary telemetry problem: air-gapped sites often block our metrics. propose a local health witness system: small operator that keeps a signed health journal stored in the site's NFS/cluster object store and operator exports 'health blobs' that redwood support can ingest when customer opts in.
maria: That preserves privacy. Also: gating rules for canary: 1) successful verification on all nodes, 2) successful smoke tests (process up, KV cache warm, sample inference ok), 3) no disk or memory regressions vs baseline.
kevin: Add a 'safety leash' policy: if more than X% of nodes fail verification within Y minutes, abort global rollout automatically.
dave: For time/skew: require bundle timestamps to be within a leeway window AND include a monotonic sequence number stored in a local ledger that agent keeps. Reject replayed sequence numbers.
sachin: For KMS/HSM reliance: offline mode should allow signing proof via short-lived ephemeral tokens derived from a local customer root-of-trust. we need a documented key-rotation UX for on-prem ops.
olivia: UX note: operators will want a `redwoodctl` offline mode. draft example:

```
# verify bundle before apply
redwoodctl verify --bundle /mnt/patches/redwood-bundle-2024.10.tar.gz --auth external-key.pem
# apply with atomic swap
redwoodctl apply --bundle /mnt/... --staging /var/lib/redwood/staging --keep-previous 2
```

maria: love that. let's add a `--dry-run --validate-only` that performs full verification and smoke run without switching pointers.
kevin: Edge-case: partially applied DB migrations. need migration idempotency and a migration rollback plan. any migration must be able to run twice or have compensating step.
dave: Agreed. enforce DB migrations ship in a sandboxed transaction where possible and if not, include compensating migration instructions in the manifest.\nanita: Operational flow for support: if rollback required and customer doesn't expose telemetry, we still need an out-of-band checklist and tooling to generate logs to review locally. document it in runbook.
maria: Action items:
- sachin: draft dual-signature validation logic + sequence ledger design (owner)
- kevin: design low-disk streaming verify & integrity journal
- olivia: sketch redwoodctl offline commands + UX
- dave: migration guidelines + compensating migrations RFC section
- anita: add canary witness health journal design + runbook checklist

please ping if any objections or if I've missed a major risk.
kevin: no objections, but add 'supply chain compromise during staging' — maybe make staging ephemeral and require signed manifest fetched directly from customer supplied airgap mirror rather than copying from random USB.
sachin: noted. I'll incorporate mirror provenance into the draft.
maria: cool — aim to have PR for the design doc by EOD Friday. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
